stances_toward.note: Tashkent is the most active Central Asian partner without recognition: the Trans-Afghan railway feasibility agreement with Pakistan (Kabul, 17 Jul 2025, ratified by Uzbekistan in February 2026), the Hairatan-Mazar-e-Sharif line contract extended in January 2026, bilateral trade of about USD 1.7bn in 2025 (Afghan outlets; unverified), a water-sharing framework with Balkh in May 2025. The friction is the Qosh Tepa canal: Kabul says no agreement limits Amu Darya withdrawals and Tashkent seeks urgent water talks - which keeps the grade at partner and not ally.

stances_toward.note: Bound by the Treaty on Allied Relations signed in Tashkent on 22 Dec 2022 together with a border demarcation agreement (Uzbekistan ratified on 30 Nov 2023, Kazakhstan's Senate on 25 Apr 2024); it covers political, trade, transit and energy cooperation and security coordination against terrorism and extremism, with no mutual-defence clause that sources mention, which is why some would read it as a partnership; the treaty's own title and the foreign ministry's 'strategic tandem' wording are the readings used. Mirziyoyev was in Astana in April 2026 and Kazakhstan's foreign minister in Tashkent in March 2026. Uzbekistan is outside the CSTO, so the two are allied in Central Asia but not in the same alliance. Bond - kin: Turkic, shared Soviet and Central Asian history.

It is a connectivity bet with an unreliable middle: no 2026 progress is verified and the Pakistan-Taliban war runs along the route. Bond - none: interest in a route to the sea.

stances_toward.note: Normalisation after the 2009-16 embargoes: Mirziyoyev's 2018 visit reopened ten border crossings and the Termez-Bokhtar railway (9 Mar 2018), and Uzbekistan dropped its opposition to Rogun. Since then it is a treaty partner (Treaty on Allied Relations, 18 Apr 2024, not a defence pact) and a power and transit partner. The 2025 Kyrgyz-Tajik border settlement was credited to Tashkent's mediation (UZB card). Bond - none: pure interest in water, power and transit, not kinship. Trend warming from the 2016-18 low; no source calls it a rivalry now (grade by structure, not rhetoric).

stances_toward.note: The gas customer next door: Turkmenistan supplies up to 2 bcm a year to Uzbekistan under the 2023 agreement. Frictions are real and old: the Amu Darya water sharing and the shared Kokdumalak condensate field (Jamestown, older analysis). We found no 2025-2026 report of a water or border agreement. Bond - affinity: Turkic, Central Asian and Muslim, sympathy without a shared state project. Trend warming on the gas track only.
